title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of CdTe growth (process)
action: Run a kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of CdTe (100) growth at 450 K with a Cd flux of 1 ML/s, using the Cd migration and evaporation rates from the paper (Table I), to evolve the surface bonding configurations and record the time evolution of kink site fractions ((2,6) and (2,7) site types). This step documents the surface roughness evolution discussed in the paper.
description: Produces a trace of the fraction of surface sites in (2,6) and (2,7) bonding configurations as a function of monolayer growth, demonstrating the variable kink site density.

title: Compute site‑specific Hg incorporation probabilities and enhancement ratios
action: Using the paper’s Hg evaporation rates (Table II) at 450 K and a specified Hg flux J_Hg, compute the occupation probability P_Hg for the (2,4), (2,6), and (2,7) site types via P_Hg = J_Hg / R_v(E_tot). Then calculate the ratios P_Hg(2,6)/P_Hg(2,4) and P_Hg(2,7)/P_Hg(2,4). Write the results as a JSON file with keys p_Hg_24, p_Hg_26, p_Hg_27, ratio_26_24, ratio_27_24.
description: JSON file containing the site‑specific incorporation probabilities and the computed enhancement ratios. This directly addresses the paper’s main claim that Hg incorporation at kink/step sites can be up to ~100× larger than at terrace sites.
